title: Terahertz fingerprints and machine learning for complementary discrimination of medicinal materials
core_motivation: THz and machine learning as complementary medicinal-material discrimination with controlled evidence to guide further materials
contributions: An audited classification-oriented coefficient-stability selector with across-class Euclidean scores, explicit final variable budgets and training-confined inner SVM selection
Matched feature-budget and retained-variable evidence for representation choices
Support-label and pipeline ablations distinguishing effective updates from tested alternative explanations
Qualified molecular frequency reference supporting interpretation

verification.reference: World Health Organization. Quality control methods for herbal materials. World Health Organization; 2011. Accessed November 15, 2026. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241500739
verification.verification: WHO publication page confirms title, publication date 5 June 2011, institutional author and ISBN. Publisher lists 187 pages; omit pagination in citation. Linked PDF is currently 403 through the browsing fetcher, so no claim is based on newly extracted PDF text.
verification.supports: Official methodological context for herbal-material quality control; combine with existing Hong Kong monograph and Raclariu2018 for the specific routine-identification methods.
verification.suggested_sentence: Established herbal-material quality-control frameworks use morphological examination and chemical testing as complementary sources of identity and quality information.
verification.scope_limit: WHO guidance is not itself a current Chinese pharmacopoeial monograph and does not establish the absence of THz from every pharmacopoeia.

verification.verification: Crossref author/title/volume/issue/pages match publisher. Wiley issue year and PubMed both confirm 2018; 2017 is the early-online date. Full publisher text inspected, especially abstract and analytical-challenges sections.
verification.supports: Most direct support for the user motivation: the article explicitly describes prevailing authentication as morphology and pharmacopoeial analytical phytochemistry; it discusses TLC/HPTLC/HPLC plus complementary DNA methods and their specific roles.
verification.suggested_sentence: Routine authentication of herbal products relies primarily on morphological examination and pharmacopoeial phytochemical methods, while additional analytical approaches can contribute complementary evidence.
verification.scope_limit: The prevailing-practice statement describes the reviewed framework; do not convert it into an exhaustive legal claim that THz is excluded from all standards or is universally inferior to established methods.
